content.title: What is a Trump Account? Rules, Taxes, and How They Work for Families | ACTEC
content.text: Trump Accounts are a new savings vehicle for children introduced in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025. Designed to encourage long-term investment, these accounts may include a $1,000 federal seed contribution and offer tax-deferred growth. Before opening one, however, families and advisors should understand how these accounts work, who qualifies, and the potential tax implications. This video explains the key features of Trump Accounts, including eligibility requirements, contribution limits, how the $1,000 government contribution works, and when beneficiaries gain control of the funds. The discussion also compares Trump Accounts with other savings options such as 529 plans, UTMAs (Uniform Transfers to Minors Act accounts), and Roth IRAs, helping families and advisors evaluate which strategies may be most appropriate.
